newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says Doe Run has until Sept to buy La Oroya.
newsitem.headline: Peru says Doe Run has until Sept to buy La Oroya.

text.p: Peruvian privatization officials said Monday Doe Run Co had until September to decide if it will buy state-owned La Oroya metallurgic complex following the decision by Mexico's Penoles to withdraw its offer.

"Penoles had two months to decide. It's fair that Doe Run should have the same period, that is to say until the end of September more or less," said Juan Barcellos, president of state miner Centromin's privatization committee.

Doe Run, the largest integrated lead producer in the United States and a subsidiary of Renco Group of New York, was runner-up to Penoles in an April 18 auction for rights to La Oroya. Doe Run had offered $121 million at the sell-off.

Penoles surprised the mining world last week by abandoning plans to acquire a 60 percent stake in the complex "because the requirements that Penoles had set to guarantee adequate profitability did not come together."

La Oroya lies in the country's central Andes 12,300 feet (3,700 meters) above sea level and 120 miles (190 km) east of Lima. The complex of refineries and smelters processes 22 metals and their by-products.
Centromin's asset sales are part of its continued piecemeal privatization, which is set to continue with the auction of more mines, hydroelectric plants and polymetallic mineral.
